# Toronto 2-Bedroom Lease Negotiation Checklist

For a **2-bedroom apartment in Toronto** at **CAD 2,850/month**, a **12-month lease**, and **move-in on 2026-06-01**, the main goals are to confirm the lease is lawful, reduce upfront cost where possible, and lock in any repair promises before signing.

## Lease Terms to Verify Before You Sign

- **Rent amount and inclusions**
  - Confirm the base rent is **CAD 2,850** and ask what is included: heat, water, hydro, internet, parking, locker, and laundry.
- **Lease start and possession**
  - Verify the lease start date matches **2026-06-01** and that you get keys, access fobs, and move-in instructions on day one.
- **Deposit terms**
  - In Ontario, landlords typically can ask for a **last month’s rent deposit** and a **key deposit** only, not a large damage/security deposit.
- **Rent increase timing**
  - Check whether the unit is rent-controlled and whether any increase would follow Ontario rules after the lease term.
- **Repairs and maintenance**
  - Make sure any promised repairs are written into the lease or a signed addendum, including timing and responsibility.
- **Utilities and services**
  - Clarify who pays each utility and whether any service interruptions or restrictions exist.
- **Assignment/sublet rights**
  - Confirm whether you may assign or sublet the unit and what approval process applies.
- **Early termination**
  - Ask whether there is a break-lease option, assignment option, or replacement tenant process.
- **Parking, pets, smoking, and guests**
  - Verify all building rules that could affect your use of the unit.
- **Condition report**
  - Request a move-in inspection checklist with photos before you accept possession.

## Questions to Ask the Landlord or Property Manager

| Topic | Question to Ask | Why It Matters |
|---|---|---|
| Deposits | What deposits are required beyond last month’s rent and key deposit? | Helps avoid unlawful or inflated upfront charges |
| Repairs | Can the needed repairs be completed before move-in, and can that be added in writing? | Protects you if the unit is not ready |
| Utilities | Which utilities are included in the rent, and which are billed separately? | Prevents surprise monthly costs |
| Rent control | Is this unit subject to Ontario rent-control rules? | Affects future rent increases |
| Move-in condition | Will you provide a signed condition report and photos at handover? | Helps protect your deposit and repair claims |
| Lease flexibility | Can the lease be assigned or sublet if my plans change? | Gives you an exit path |
| Access | How many keys/fobs are included, and what is the replacement fee? | Avoids extra move-in costs |
| Maintenance | What is the response time for urgent repairs and routine maintenance? | Sets expectations for service |

## Negotiation Points That Fit This Rental

- **Lower upfront deposit**
  - Ask to limit the deposit to **last month’s rent + key deposit only**.
- **Repair completion before move-in**
  - Request that all current issues be fixed before **2026-06-01**.
- **Rent concessions**
  - If repairs are delayed, ask for a **small rent credit** or a **free first week**.
- **Included services**
  - Negotiate for **parking**, **internet**, or **one utility** to be included if the rent is firm.
- **Lease clarity**
  - Ask for a written addendum confirming any promised work, appliance replacements, or cleaning.

## Short Message to Request Repairs and a Lower Deposit

Hello [Landlord/Property Manager],

I’m very interested in the apartment and would like to move forward, but I noticed a few items that need repair before move-in on **2026-06-01**. Could you please confirm that these will be completed before handover and added to the lease or an addendum in writing?

Also, I’d like to ask whether the upfront deposit can be limited to the standard **last month’s rent deposit and key deposit only**. If that works, I’m happy to proceed promptly.

Thank you,
[Your Name]

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Standard Lease Form](https://www.ontario.ca/page/guide-ontarios-standard-lease)

- Ontario standard lease guide: https://www.ontario.ca/page/guide-ontarios-standard-lease
- Toronto tenant support: https://www.torontotenants.org/
